summary: Skagit County lookout in the Mount Baker-Snoqualmie NF: a 1928 cupola, a current R-6 cab dated 1961 to 1967, open to the public with first-come overnight stays.

facts.design: Live-in 15x15-ft R-6 flat-roof cab on a 30-ft treated timber tower

access.note: Open to the public year round; access limited by road and trail conditions; first-come overnight stays; recreation pass required per vehicle; catwalk limited to two people per side.

visit.trail_note: Lookout Mountain-Monogram Lake Trail 743: 3.5 miles through timber, then 1.2 miles of meadows (Forest Service). TrailChick gives just over 4.5 miles one way and calls the upper slope a major avalanche hazard, with winter attempts possible only with extreme caution.

notes_for_editor: Construction dates conflict: first lookout 1928 (register, TrailChick) vs 1929 (Forest Service, firelookout.com); current tower 1961 (firelookout), 1962 (register Built field, Forest Service) and 1967 (register cab note, TrailChick, which calls 1967 the current structure). The story gives the range rather than picking one. Elevation conflicts (register 5,631 ft; firelookout 5,719 ft; Forest Service 5,700 ft); the brief's 1716.3 m matches the register. Staffing evidence is only the register's 2008 visit report; no current staffing source was found. The 9.1 m height is a conversion of firelookout's 30-ft figure. TrailChick's 2024 update and 2017 visit describe the trail as overgrown in 2017, which is not used in the story.
